stem: Incidence refers to which epidemiologic quantity?

options.label: A
options.text: New cases in a population over a defined period
options.misconception: None — incidence counts only new cases arising during a specified period.
options.explanation: Incidence refers to the occurrence of new cases of disease or injury in a population over a specified period of time.

options.label: B
options.text: All existing cases in a population at one point in time
options.misconception: Confuses incidence (new cases) with prevalence (all existing cases).
options.explanation: Existing cases at one point in time define point prevalence, which counts long-standing and new cases alike rather than only new ones.

options.label: C
options.text: Deaths in a population over a defined period
options.misconception: Confuses the occurrence of new disease with the occurrence of death.
options.explanation: Deaths in a population over a defined period give the mortality rate, which measures dying rather than developing disease.

options.label: D
options.text: Deaths from the disease among all people who have it
options.misconception: Confuses incidence with case-fatality, which uses cases as its denominator.
options.explanation: Deaths from a disease among all people who have it is the case-fatality rate, a measure of disease severity.

options.label: E
options.text: Risk among exposed people relative to risk among unexposed people
options.misconception: Confuses a measure of disease frequency with a measure of association.
options.explanation: Risk in exposed relative to unexposed people is the risk ratio, a measure of association rather than of disease occurrence.

context: Learning objective: Incidence is the occurrence of new cases of disease or injury in a population over a specified period of time.
